descriptor.anonymous: A stream of adult commuters in late-1990s and 2000s office clothes walking past, briefcases and coffee cups, and one odd young person in a t-shirt stepping through the door. None is a canon character.
descriptor.scene: A stream of five or six adult commuters is the subject, walking left to right along an ordinary city sidewalk past the plain honey-brown door, which stands open a little in the brick-and-plaster wall with warm light through the gap. Every commuter looks straight ahead, not one of them glancing at it. One young person in a t-shirt and jeans, mid-stride, is halfway through the doorway into the light. The commuters fill the middle band of the frame at full length. If the sidewalk is empty of people the image is wrong. Keep the bottom right calmer than the rest. The door leaf has EXACTLY FOUR recessed panels in TWO rows and no more: a top row of two small square panels, and below it a single row of two tall rectangular panels that reach nearly to the floor with only a plain flat rail beneath them. There is NO third row of panels at the bottom of the door.
negatives: anyone in the crowd looking at the door
signage or readable text on the street
anything visible through the gap other than warm light
a six-panel colonial door, a third row of panels at the bottom of the door leaf
descriptor._caption: It looked like a toy. Most people walked past it on the way to real jobs. A few odd ones walked through. Nobody labeled the door.
